summary: High-concurrency quantized-model kernel fallback causing elevated 5xx rate and runtime GPU resets
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12T13:20 UTC, a single dedicated-tenant (NarrativeLabs) observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the Redwood API. Impact: Customer facing failures for generation and embedding requests (~15-25% 5xx rate at peak) and elevated tail latency. Root-cause (short): Under sustained high concurrency to a pinned int8 quantized model, the runtime's kernel selector occasionally failed to pick the quantized kernel for long sequence lengths and fell back to a float kernel. The float fallback significantly increased per-request GPU memory, causing memory fragmentation and NVML watchdog resets on a subset of GPUs which in turn produced upstream runtime exits and amplified API gateway 502/503s. This ticket tracks the customer report, investigation, mitigation, and postmortem action items.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Pin tenant to model nl-vq-1.2-int8 in Dedicated pool
2) Send concurrent streaming generation requests with sequence lengths ranging 1k-4k tokens from 200 parallel clients
3) Observe runtime kernel selection logs and GPU memory footprints
4) Repeat with similar concurrency against fp16 variant for baseline comparison
observed_behavior: API gateway returned elevated 5xx rates (502/503) and streaming disconnects. Runtime health checks recorded NVML watchdog resets (driver timeouts) on 2/12 GPUs in the tenant pool. Kernel-selector logs show intermittent 'kernel_not_found' events followed by 'fallback_to_fp32' for batches that earlier had quantized kernels. P99 latency increased from ~450ms to >3.2s at peak.
expected_behavior: Kernel selector should consistently choose quantized/int8 kernels for supported model shapes and sequence lengths under the pinned model. GPU memory per request should remain at quantified int8 footprints and not escalate to fp32-sized allocations causing fragmentation or watchdog resets.
logs_and_metrics: apigw.5xx_rate: spike from 0.6% -> 18% between 2026-03-12T13:20 and 13:40 UTC
gpu.nvml_watchdog_resets: 2 reset events on worker ids w-54, w-77
gpu.mem_usage.per_request: int8 ~1.2GB -> fallback fp32 ~4.8GB (per large request)
investigation_notes: 13:30 UTC - Support triage: customer reported immediate impact after a scheduled high-throughput test; tickets opened and SLA escalated to P1.
13:36 UTC - Observed correlation between request size distribution (heavy >1k token requests) and kernel_selector 'kernel_not_found' events in runtime logs.

13:45 UTC - Confirmed kernel selector falls back to fp32 kernels when a combined condition is met: quantized kernel build missing for specific sequence length and batch alignment under concurrent access.
13:50 UTC - NVML resets followed fallback events by ~10-30s; memory graphs show fragmentation (many small free blocks) rather than contiguous free region for allocation.

14:05 UTC - Reproduced locally on a staging shard by simulating tenant traffic; reproduced kernel_missing -> fallback -> increased memory -> simulated watchdog timeout via constrained driver timeout setting.

14:30 UTC - Mitigation plan agreed: temporary tenant-side throttling + rollback of model pin (pointed to fp16 variant) while engineering implements a runtime kernel selector fix and conservative allocation guard.

Engineering hypothesis: bug in kernel selection cache eviction under high concurrency leads to a race where a quantized kernel entry is considered unavailable and fallback path increments allocation size without triggering aggressive eviction/defragmentation.
actions_taken: 14:40 UTC - Support applied temporary rate cap for NarrativeLabs (reduced concurrency by ~70%) via tenant policy -> immediate drop in 5xx to <2%
15:05 UTC - Customer agreed to unpin model and switch to nl-vq-1.2-fp16 fallback for the remainder of the business day
15:40 UTC - Autoscaler tuned: added soft headroom for the affected Dedicated pool to reduce per-GPU pressure during sudden high parallelism
16:10 UTC - Rollforward patch deployed to kernel-selector (hotfix) that adds a concurrency-safe kernel cache lookup, with feature flag off by default
16:30 UTC - Enabled hotfix under feature flag for a single staging shard and gradually rolled to affected Dedicated pool; observed no further kernel_not_found events and no new NVML resets
resolution: Root cause: concurrency race in runtime kernel-selector caused quantized kernels to appear missing for certain sequence/batch shapes; fallback to fp32 kernels increased per-request GPU memory causing fragmentation and NVML watchdog resets. Resolution steps: 1) Immediate customer mitigation (throttling + switch to fp16 variant) reduced customer impact. 2) Hotfix to kernel-selector (concurrency-safe cache lookup and an allocation guard) deployed and verified in affected pool. 3) Added a runtime alert for kernel_not_found spike and automated tenant-level soft-throttling recommendation when per-GPU memory pressure >75%. Follow-ups include a postmortem and a stress test suite covering mixed-length sequences under high concurrency. Incident closed after 24h of stable metrics post-fix.
